content:
I made, with LLM help, some useful-to-me bits of PGF machinery. It is at https://github.com/genneth/lean-branching-processes. Feedback welcome!

Background: I was a physicist back in the day, and during my PhD I did some work on branching processes. Thought it might be nice to go back and formalise what little mathematics I did do, and found myself needing some PGF machinery that didn't yet exist in mathlib.

Hi Gen Zhang,
I appreciate the want-to-contribute, and thanks for up-front highlighting the LLM usage :smile: . It is the rules to do so, but many don't.

I have limited knowledge of branching processes and I truly have no idea about their implementation in lean. However, I have done some PRs before so can at least give you some feedback in that direction:

  1. I see in your Github multiple files. Making a PR of them in one go and trying them to get accepted, will not fly. You need to cut it up in smaller bit. A start would be for example the file GaltonWatson/Basic.lean.
  2. Your proofs are not completely up to the standard quality that is expected (nothing to be ashamed of! we all started of that way). To give an example, abel_solution_unique is quite long and has a lot of have's. Typically, these are shortened by making clever use of tactics like simp or calc. The ones in GaltonWatson/Basic.lean seem largely fine.

Sorry for not being to help better.
